metadata.title: Calisthenics Alliance
metadata.description: The Portuguese endurance calisthenics league. 1v1 Battles, a national ranking, and a final to decide the best athlete of the year.

hero.subtitle: The Portuguese endurance calisthenics league. 1v1 Battles, a national ranking, and a final to decide the best athlete of the year.
hero.countdownLive: It's today. See you at the arena.

nextEvent.title: Open CAL
nextEvent.lead: One routine for every athlete in the League. Your result sets your competitive division and your starting position in the national ranking.

pillars.title: Three pillars
pillars.lead: CAL was created to answer the absence of a regular, continuous and properly regulated competitive structure for Endurance in Portugal.

items.title: A continuous structure
items.body: A season with no shortage of events: an opening ceremony, four regular Rounds and a Grand Final.

items.title: Rigorous judging
items.body: A National Judging Committee applying uniform criteria. Full range of motion, mandatory lockout, zero kipping.

items.title: A ranking with purpose
items.body: Every Battle counts. Base points plus performance bonuses, in a national ranking per category and division.

season.title: From the opening to the title
season.lead: Three phases, one season. Athletes accumulate points through the regular season and the best of them fight for the title at the Grand Final.

phases.title: Open CAL
phases.body: The opening event, mandatory for every registered athlete. It determines each athlete's division and starting rank.

phases.title: 4 Rounds
phases.body: The regular season. 1v1 Battles within each category and division. Every athlete is called up for three/four Rounds.

phases.title: Grand Final
phases.body: A knockout bracket with the top eight of each category and division. It determines the season champion.

divisions.title: Compete against your level
divisions.lead: Two categories and up to three divisions. Each division with its own routines, call-ups, ranking and prizes.

items.name: Elite
items.body: Top athletes with extensive competitive experience and advanced command of the technical and physical requirements.

items.name: Advanced
items.body: Athletes with some competitive experience and solid command of the technical and physical requirements.

items.name: Promises
items.body: Recreational athletes, or those at the start of a competitive path, focused on progress and experience.

divisions.note: Your division is assigned from your Open CAL result and stays fixed for the whole season.

scoring.title: Winning matters
scoring.lead: Every Battle awards points, even in defeat. Winning matters most, but it is your time that sets you apart from athletes on similar results.
scoring.bonusBody: Up to 30 points, distributed by total execution time.
scoring.bonusLegend: N = eligible athletes · P = position by time/division

partners.title: Built with the community
partners.lead: CAL is organised together with clubs, athletes and organisations from across the Portuguese calisthenics community.

meta.title: The League
meta.description: Calisthenics Alliance is an Endurance-focused calisthenics league organised by Associação B.W.C.R. — Clube de Calistenia das Caldas da Rainha.

hero.title: A league for Endurance
hero.lead: Calisthenics Alliance is a project created by Associação B.W.C.R. — Clube de Calistenia das Caldas da Rainha, together with other clubs, athletes and organisations from the Portuguese calisthenics community, to organise, regulate and promote competitive calisthenics in Portugal.

story.title: Why now
story.body: Calisthenics in Portugal keeps growing, but it had no regular, continuous, properly regulated competitive structure for Endurance. CAL rests on three pillars: a uniform and continuous competitive structure, a rigorous and impartial judging system, and a classification model that gives the season purpose, progression and commitment.

objectives.title: What we set out to do
items: Create a uniform, continuous competitive structure
Raise the technical and physical level of athletes through regular competition
Establish a national ranking for Endurance
Promote safe practice and athletes' physical integrity
Build a cohesive, active and lasting community around the discipline

format.title: How the season is contested
format.battleBody: In the regular-season Rounds, two athletes of the same category and division perform the same routine simultaneously. Whoever completes the routine in the least time wins.
format.routineBody: Each routine defines the exercises and their order, the repetitions, any added load, and the timecap. It's published at least 30 days in advance.
format.callupBody: Pairings are set manually by the organisation, based on proximity in the ranking. The same two athletes never meet twice in the same regular season.
format.finalBody: The top eight of each category and division qualify — or the top four in divisions with fewer than eight athletes. A knockout bracket, with no ranking points.

judging.title: Always the same criteria
judging.body: The National Judging Committee (CNJ) keeps validation criteria uniform across every event. Decisions on the validity of a repetition are immediate, final and binding — there is no video review, and no appeal during execution.
criteria: Lockout at the start and end of the movement
No kipping — no swing or momentum

regulation.title: Internal Regulation
regulation.body: Everything on this site is a summary. The official document covers registration, eligibility, event protocol, technical rules, judging, scoring, the Grand Final, discipline and data protection.
regulation.onlyPt: The regulation is available in Portuguese only.

meta.title: Open CAL
meta.description: The opening event of the Calisthenics Alliance. {date}, Pavilhão Desportivo Rainha D. Leonor, Caldas da Rainha. For all levels.

hero.title: Open CAL
hero.subtitle: One routine. One packed room. The moment when the season starts.

what.title: The start of the season
what.body: Open CAL is the league's opening event, and taking part is mandatory for every registered athlete. You perform a single competitive routine, different for each category. The result determines the division you'll compete in all season and your starting position in the national ranking.

highlights.title: One routine
highlights.body: A single competitive routine per category, published at least 30 days in advance.

highlights.title: One field
highlights.body: There are no divisions: at Open CAL every athlete in the same category competes together.

highlights.title: No points
highlights.body: Open CAL awards no points. It sets your division and your starting position in the ranking.

highlights.title: For all levels
highlights.body: You don't have to be able to finish the routine. Your division is based on what you do complete.

classification.title: How you're ranked
classification.lead: Criteria are applied in this order, until the tie is broken.
items: A draw held by the organisation at the end of the event
classification.note: Athletes are placed in descending order and split evenly across the open divisions, each of which holds an even number of athletes.

steps.title: Arrival
steps.body: You're advised to be at the competition area 30 minutes before your routine is scheduled.

steps.title: Warm-up
steps.body: Every athlete warms up on their own, outside the competition area, on a space designated by the organisation.

steps.title: Call-up
steps.body: After the call you get 5 minutes to prepare, and a maximum 10-minute grace period to present yourself.

steps.title: Execution
steps.body: Exercises are performed in the prescribed order. Their execution only has to be unbroken if the routine says so.

steps.title: Timecap
steps.body: After the time limit expires, execution stops and the result is recorded, even if the routine was not completed.

special.title: The rule unique to Open CAL
special.body: If you can't start or finish the repetitions of an exercise, you can finish it early and proceed to the next one, informing the judge of your decision. Valid repetitions up to that transition count. The decision is irreversible.

exercises.title: Exercise list
exercises.lead: CAL routines may include the following exercises. Every repetition requires full range of motion, lockout, controlled movement and zero kipping.

equipment.title: What you can bring
allowed: Solid or liquid chalk, brought by you
Your own weight belt (chain or strap)
Wrist wraps, tape and joint support
forbidden: Resins, glues and other grip aids
Your own plates and weight vests
Hook grips, suspension hooks and any strap fixing you to the bar

meta.title: Registration
meta.description: Register for the Calisthenics Alliance {season} season. Fourteen and over, all levels welcome.

hero.title: Registration
hero.lead: One registration covers the whole season: Open CAL, the Rounds of the regular season and, if you qualify, the Grand Final.

items.title: Fill in the form
items.body: The athlete form, including the team you represent — club, gym, or none at all.

items.title: Pay the fee
items.body: Your registration is only confirmed once the season fee has been paid.

items.title: Show up at Open CAL
items.body: Sign the liability waiver and the declaration of fitness, and come compete.

fee.title: Registration fee

installments.title: By Open CAL
installments.body: First instalment, paid after you register.

installments.title: By the 1st Round
installments.body: Second instalment, paid before the regular season starts.

fee.support: Struggling with paying the fee or need special terms? Talk to us before the deadline — we look at every case.
includes: Place in the national ranking for your category and division
Access to the league's official communication group

payment.title: How to pay
payment.proof: Always send the proof of payment to <link>{tel}</link>.

eligibility.title: Who can compete
items: Be properly registered in the league
Be up to date with the payment deadlines
Be 14 or older by the date of Open CAL

items.title: Admitted in pairs
items.body: There's a maximum number of athletes per category and admission always happens in pairs. Anyone beyond it joins a waiting list.

items.title: Withdrawal
items.body: You're fully refunded if you withdraw up to the day before Open CAL. After that, no refund is due.

items.title: Division not opened
items.body: If no division suited to your level opens, or your category is cancelled, you're refunded in full.

items.title: Cancellation
items.body: If the season is cancelled before Open CAL, the refund is full. After it, the refund is proportional to the events not held.

cta.title: Claim your place
cta.lead: Places per category are limited, and the waiting list runs in registration order. Don't wait until the last minute!
cta.note: Questions? Talk to us before you register

meta.title: National Ranking
meta.description: The Calisthenics Alliance national ranking, by category and division.

hero.title: National Ranking
hero.lead: The ranking is calculated independently for each category and division, and updated within 72 hours of every Round.

empty.title: The ranking starts after Open CAL
empty.body: Until the first Round, each division's ranking is the classification obtained at Open CAL. Come back on {date}.

how.title: The points system
how.bonusBody: Athletes who finish the routine within the timecap are ordered by total time. The bonus goes up to 30 points and is calculated for each Round, per category and division.
